solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sailors almost smell the moon above?!

indicators.note: almost means the word for the sailors loses its final letter

parts.note: a ship's crew are its sailors
a scent is a smell

explanation.surface: Seafarers nearly catch a whiff of the moon overhead, an absurd sensory image.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin curved sliver is how the moon often appears in the night sky, so this shape names it.

clue.text: Feature of bath taps? Two letters on them, see!

parts.note: taps are usually marked C for cold and H for hot
Rome is the Holy See, the seat of the Pope

explanation.surface: Pointing out the letters stamped on bathroom taps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like look, but it is a bishop's seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Taps are commonly plated with this shiny metal finish, so it is a feature of them.

clue.text: Old lover, criticised audibly, put on weight?

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: audibly means the criticised word is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: panned means harshly criticised, as by reviewers

explanation.surface: A former partner, mocked for having gained weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow larger or fill out is to put on weight in the sense of getting bigger.

clue.text: Author's name held in little credit

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the name word is held inside the credit letters

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit
a handle is a name, especially a nickname

explanation.surface: An author's name appears in the small print of the credits.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was the American writer of the Philip Marlowe detective novels.

clue.text: Adolescent turning up is one regrettably under-occupied?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent

explanation.surface: A teenager who turns up is sadly at a loose end.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a British acronym: Not in Education, Employment or Training.
explanation.definitionFit: A young person with no job, schooling or training is sadly idle, the very picture of under-occupied.

clue.text: A fellow crossing a river on a ferry?

indicators.note: the fellow word straddles the other letters, holding them within it

parts.note: bod is informal British slang for a person or fellow

explanation.surface: A man making his way over a river on a ferry boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'A' is the article used as written; the second 'a' joins R inside BOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried on a vessel as a passenger is being on board, the adverb for travelling on it.

clue.text: Prohibition — no climbing tree

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the word reads upwards

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: A ban: no climbing the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an Indian fig tree whose branches send down roots that become new trunks.

clue.text: A cinema star's latest possibly from Hollywood?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way
the latest of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A film star's newest release may come from Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' picks R, the last letter of star's (the 's set aside); it joins A and CINEMA in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Hollywood is in the United States, so anything from there is of that nationality.

clue.text: Planned performance full of offence — little good in it

indicators.note: the performance word is filled with the other letters

parts.note: a deed is a feat, a performance of an action

indicators.note: it refers to the offence, so the good letter goes inside that word

parts.note: a sin is an offence
G is the short form of good

explanation.surface: A deliberate act of offending, with only a trace of goodness in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little good in it' makes SIGN; that then goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worked out in advance has been deliberately planned, a synonym.

clue.text: Ring discovered in grass set aside

indicators.note: the ring word is found sitting inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A ring found in the grass is put to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that has been revoked or annulled is set aside, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Thrones maybe set in an entrance to schloss

indicators.note: the set word sits inside the letters formed by an and the first letter of schloss
the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does

explanation.surface: Royal thrones placed at the doorway of a German castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Thrones are one of the nine orders of the celestial hierarchy, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In traditional theology Thrones are one rank of heavenly beings, an example of the wider group.

clue.text: Ostentatious relative in hurry

indicators.note: the relative word goes into the hurry word

parts.note: to fly is to hurry
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A showy relative rushing about.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclined to show off, flaunting things, is an informal word for showy.

clue.text: Song that's mournful, gloomy, with any number joining in

indicators.note: the number letter joins in, entering the middle of the gloomy word

parts.note: moody means gloomy, sullen
N is the mathematical symbol for any number

explanation.surface: A sad song, gloomy, which any number of people join in singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament or dirge sung by a single voice, often for the dead, is this kind of mournful poem or song.

clue.text: Member gets to stick around in open space

indicators.note: the sticking word goes around the member word

parts.note: to cling is to stick fast
an ear is a member, or organ, of the body

explanation.surface: A club member manages to hang around in an open area.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch of land cleared of trees in a wood is an open space within it.

clue.text: What Nell Gwyn managed to do, sending a cheeky signal?

definitions.text: What Nell Gwyn managed to do
definitions.meaning: Nell Gwyn became mistress of Charles II, winning over a monarch, so split it reads as two words
closing one eye briefly as a playful sign

explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was an actress and mistress of King Charles II of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two it describes Nell Gwyn capturing Charles II's heart; whole, it is shutting one eye flirtatiously.

clue.text: Fairy Queen with little energy is a weedy type

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology
E is the physics symbol for energy, a little version of the word

explanation.surface: Spenser's Faerie Queene with little energy, a feeble character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weedy' looks like feeble, but the weed is tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a strong dark tobacco from Louisiana, and tobacco is jokingly called the weed.

clue.text: Hack stone

definitions.meaning: a hack is a worn-out old horse, a nag
a green gemstone used for carving

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a broken-down nag and a hard green ornamental mineral.

clue.text: Cow is in fear, having been disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are jumbled out of their order

explanation.surface: A cow is frightened after being disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cow' looks like a verb meaning intimidate, beside fear, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black-and-white breed of dairy cattle, an example of a cow.

clue.text: Drunk returned shortly to join chorus

indicators.note: shortly means the returned word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: back means returned
a chant is a chorus sung together

explanation.surface: A drunk returns quickly to join in the singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Bacchus is a drunken reveller, so the noun suits a drunk.

clue.text: Odd bods long restricted by barriers

indicators.note: the long word is hemmed in by the barriers word

parts.note: weirs are barriers across rivers
to be dying for something is to long for it, so die means long

explanation.surface: Eccentric people kept penned in behind barriers for a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange or eccentric people are informally called odd bods, a synonym for weirdos.

clue.text: Den gone over for a bit of money

indicators.note: gone over means the den word is turned back on itself

parts.note: a lair is an animal's den

explanation.surface: A den searched thoroughly for a few coins.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a currency unit of Iran, Oman and Yemen, so a piece of money.

clue.text: Scamper as childminder — kiddiewink finally tucked in

indicators.note: the child's final letter is tucked inside the childminder word

parts.note: a sitter, or babysitter, minds children

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of kiddiewink

explanation.surface: A babysitter hurries off once the little child has been tucked into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiddiewink is a British jocular word for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run lightly and quickly, the same scurrying movement as this verb.

clue.text: Appearance of Prince gatecrashing a party

indicators.note: the prince letter forces its way into the party letters

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: A prince turns up uninvited at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: The look or appearance of something is its aspect, a synonym.

clue.text: A hundred and rising — I must be hot stuff!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a hill is a rising, a piece of rising ground

explanation.surface: A temperature over a hundred and climbing: someone declares themselves hot stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' looks like a verb but is a noun, raised ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot pepper or spicy sauce is hot stuff, literally fiery to eat.

clue.text: Pet — one worshipped friend, jumping up

indicators.note: in a down entry, jumping up means the letters read upwards

parts.note: a god is one who is worshipped
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A pet adored by its owner as a friend, leaping up to greet them.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dog kept as a pampered companion is a type of pet.

clue.text: Cutting out trying to get fit maybe without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation letters are removed

parts.note: exercising is one way of trying to get fit
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Giving up a fitness regime decisively, without dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting out' looks like giving up something, but it means removing surgically.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise is to cut away, as a surgeon removes tissue, so the participle matches.

clue.text: Composer to a very large extent a god to many Indians

indicators.note: to a very large extent means nearly all of the composer's name, losing only its last letter

parts.note: Johannes Brahms was a German composer

explanation.surface: A composer revered almost as a deity by many Indian listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: This deity is the creator in the Hindu trinity, worshipped by many people in India.

clue.text: Mist in wood not beginning to lift

indicators.note: not means the beginning of lift is removed from the wood word

parts.note: hazel is a wood

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of lift

explanation.surface: Fog in a forest refusing to start clearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin mist or vapour that clouds the air is a haze, a near synonym.

clue.text: This person's taking excessively long time to get ideas

parts.note: this person is means I am, contracted to I'm
ages means a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone admits they are taking far too long to come up with ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental pictures or conceptions are ideas, a near synonym in the sense of notions.

clue.text: Baddie kept outside French town complained

indicators.note: the baddie word is kept on the outside, wrapping the town word

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a villain
ville is French for town

explanation.surface: A villain locked out of a French town grumbled about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cavil is to raise petty objections, so the past tense means found fault.

clue.text: Express in symbols message that would disappoint London's art lovers?

definitions.meaning: to write down in a system of signs, as music is written

definitions.text: message that would disappoint London's art lovers
definitions.meaning: read as two words it says there is ..., the London art gallery

explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of famous London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down in notation is to express it in symbols; split, it is a sign announcing no Tate gallery.

clue.text: US general is very cold dismissing one

indicators.note: dismissing means the one letter is sent away from the cold word

parts.note: perishing is British informal for very cold
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American general, freezing, sacks one of his officers.
explanation.definitionFit: John J. Pershing commanded the American forces in Europe in the First World War.
